listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Wednesday, October 21. Our lead story is about Elon Musk. He has confirmed that he is considering merging Tesla and SpaceX. Musk says special committees have been formed within both companies to look at a possible mega-merger. No deal has been announced. The committees are examining the idea. Now the front page. US envoy Steve Witkoff has landed in St Petersburg to discuss proposals on ending Russia's war with Ukraine. Ukrainian President Zelensky says intelligence sharing works now. In tech, Simon Willison warns that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs. In California, Los Angeles County election officials say the federal list of twenty thousand likely noncitizens registered to vote is unreliable. They say some people on it appear to be born in the United States. In health news, Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja. The patient is a woman who arrived from Uganda. Now the sections. In Tech and AI, the Claude Platform release notes say inference hooks are out of beta for Enterprise organizations. User profiles also let API platforms say which end customer a request is for. Anthropic has also published research on using Claude to reduce the attack surface of code. In Politics, Drop Site reports on Sudan drone strikes that killed more than one hundred sixty people. President Trump is expected to campaign with Senator Darline Graham, even though they disagree on Russia sanctions. In World news, France is imposing nightly curfews in Paris, Lyon and other cities. China has opened a joint airbase in Laos. Saudi Arabia has cancelled its Davos in the Desert meeting because of air strikes. In Sports, the 49ers are managing Mike Evans and his Achilles tendinitis. Next up for San Francisco is a Week 7 game against the Falcons in Atlanta. In UFC, Jasmine Jasudavicius beat Erin Blanchfield by unanimous decision. In Atlanta, MARTA's Five Points overhaul faces a growing budget and delays. A heavy vehicle hit the Moores Mill Road bridge and caused a partial collapse. The Krog District owners have bought the last missing piece along the Beltline. In Architecture, ArchDaily looks at how wastewater plants entered the city as civic buildings. It also features the M38 House, a thirty-eight square metre prefab home. In Science, NASA reports progress on the nuclear power module for its SR-1 Freedom spacecraft. Researchers also report a quantum computing step that brings the megaquops era closer. And US deep-sea mining claims in the Pacific now rival the area set aside by the international regulator. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Elon Musk confirms he is considering merging Tesla and SpaceX
lead.note: Elon Musk has confirmed that he is considering a merger of Tesla and SpaceX. According to the BBC, Musk says special committees have been formed within both companies to look at a possible mega-merger. The report does not say that a deal has been agreed. It says only that the idea is now being examined inside each company. For a reader who follows AI, space and large-scale technology, the move would join two of the best-known companies Musk is associated with. Because the committees have been formed to look at the idea, the outcome is not settled, and details such as terms, timing or structure are not given in the summary. Musk's own confirmation that the idea is under consideration is why it leads today's paper.
